Title: Syed Azman humbled, Ruzita champions PwD inclusion after receiving Maulidur Rasul awards
Article:
SERDANG: Weststar Group founder and managing director Tan Sri Dr Syed Azman Syed Ibrahim said he initially felt unqualified to receive the national-level Maulidur Rasul Tokoh Perdana award as he was not a religious scholar.
Syed Azman said he was surprised when informed of his selection and initially questioned whether he was suitable for the honour.
"I still cannot believe it. When Jakim director-general Datuk Dr Sirajuddin Suhaimee personally handed me the letter, I told him, 'I don't think I am qualified' to be a tokoh. I am not knowledgeable in religious matters.
"But he told me that if I reject this, 'you will be the first one to reject. No one will reject'. So I had to accept it. Alhamdulillah, I am grateful," he said when met with reporters today.
He thanked the government and the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (Jakim) for selecting him for the award.
Meanwhile, International Islamic University Malaysia (IIUM) Professor Dr Ruzita Mohd Amin, who received the Tokoh Wanita Madani award, said the recognition was not only for her but also for the Persons with Disabilities (PwD) community and women.
She said the award was particularly meaningful as it highlighted the need to revive Prophet Muhammad's example of showing compassion and respect towards people with disabilities and other vulnerable groups.
Ruzita said people with disabilities were still often marginalised and considered part of vulnerable groups as they were frequently overlooked in society.
"Rasulullah often showed compassion towards people with disabilities, but in today's society we see the PwD community often being marginalised.
"I feel this effort by Jakim is very timely as it brings attention back to this sunnah and shows how Islam, through the example of Rasulullah, teaches us to treat everyone well," she said.
She said every individual possessed karamah insaniah, or human dignity, regardless of whether they were from the PwD community or the B40 group.
"Every person has their dignity and honour, whether they are PwD or from the B40 group. They should be treated with respect and given opportunities.
"PwD can also succeed if they are given the right support," she said.
Ruzita said she hoped the recognition would encourage Malaysians to be more accepting of people with disabilities across all aspects of life.
She said inclusion should extend beyond education and employment to religious activities and other areas where PwD often faced barriers.
She also called for mosques to become more open and accessible to people with disabilities, saying religious institutions should ensure the PwD community could participate fully in religious activities.
Ruzita similarly urged employers to provide greater opportunities for people with disabilities, stressing that the community could achieve success when given appropriate support and opportunities.
She said the recognition should ultimately encourage society to translate the Prophet's teachings into everyday life by treating everyone with dignity, respect and compassion.

Title: Oil steadies as investors weigh impact of latest US sanctions on Iran
Article:
SINGAPORE: Oil prices recovered ground on Tuesday after settling down more than two per cent in the previous session, with investors assessing the impact of the latest US sanctions against Iran.
Brent crude futures rose 27 cents, or 0.3 per cent, to US$92.44 a barrel by 0330 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude was up 37 cents, or 0.4 per cent, at US$85.38.
Both contracts settled lower on Monday, with US crude oil falling to a one-week low on profit taking after prices rallied over the previous two weeks.
"The market seems largely unfazed by Washington's push for tighter economic pressure on Iran, with traders treating the US effort to nudge partners away from Iranian trade as marginal rather than market moving," said ING commodity strategists in a note on Tuesday.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Monday unveiled an expansion of sanctions to cut off Iran's economic lifeline, to force an end to the war between them, telling countries they would need to sever their business ties or risk being cut out of the dollar-based financial system.
However, he declined to identify the countries that would be targeted or reveal when those penalties would take effect, saying he would instead provide them time to comply with the new directive.
While US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said on Monday the U.S. would not rule out using military force against Iran, the country is turning towards more economic coercion, which analysts said removed concerns about threats to Middle Eastern oil supply because of the war.
"Markets appear to be pricing economic pressure as a lower-risk path for physical supply than kinetic action, which is why the initial reaction was for oil to move lower rather than spike higher," said Tim Waterer, chief market analyst at KCM.
However, he warned, "Iran still retains the ability to respond by disrupting shipping, which continues to keep a residual premium in the oil price."
Highlighting those threats, an oil tanker was struck on Tuesday by an unidentified projectile and disabled about 9 nautical miles (16.7 km) northeast of Oman's Ash Shishah, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations said.
Iran is still maintaining it should have control over the key Strait of Hormuz, which before the war started in February typically carried cargoes equal to about 20 per cent of global oil use. On Monday, it named 45 tankers that had broken its rules on crossing the strait and threatened action against them, including confiscating their cargoes.
The supply disruptions as a result of the US-Israeli war on Iran that started on February 28 have caused countries to draw down their commercial and strategic reserves.
On Monday, the Department of Energy reported stocks of crude oil in the US Strategic Petroleum Reserve fell by about 3.7 million barrels to 289.7 million barrels last week, the lowest since November 1982.

Title: Rahim Razali honoured with Perak Tokoh Pengamal Media award
Article:
IPOH: Film director and actor Datuk Abdul Rahim Mohd Razali received the Tokoh Pengamal Media award at the state-level Maulidur Rasul celebrations here today.
The award, Anugerah Zaid bin Thabit, was presented by Sultan of Perak Sultan Nazrin Muizzuddin Shah, who graced the celebration themed "Fostering Muslim Character — Fortifying the Identity of the Ummah" at a hotel here.
Sultan Nazrin, who arrived at 11am, was accompanied by Raja Permaisuri Perak Tuanku Zara Salim.
Also present were Raja Muda Perak Raja Jaafar Raja Muda Musa, Raja DiHilir Perak Raja Iskandar Dzulkarnain Idris Shah and Perak Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad.
Abdul Rahim, 87, from Batu Gajah, launched his career as a broadcasting assistant with Radio Malaysia (RTM). He also founded his own production company, Angkatan Seniman Abad XX Sdn Bhd, in 1981.
He was also a scriptwriter and drama director in Australia and produced 50 dramas for RTM and 15 films, eight of which were selected for the Tokyo International Film Festival.
He was also interviewed for the documentary The Untold Truth About Supermokh, which was broadcast on National Geographic on Aug 30, 2010.
Better known by his stage name Rahim Razali, Abdul Rahim directed and starred in iconic films including Abang (1981), Matinya Seorang Patriot (1984) and Tsu Feh Sofiah (1986).
He also appeared in more recent films, including Munafik (2016) and Imaginur (2023).
He received RM5,000 and a plaque with the award.
The celebration also saw the presentation of the Tokoh Keluarga Mithali award, Anugerah Keluarga Ammar bin Yasir, to Yang Walad, 82, from Kuala Kurau.
Yang, a mother of 15, received RM10,000, an Umrah package worth RM9,000 and a plaque.
Sultan Nazrin also presented the Tokoh Pendakwah award (Anugerah Ibnu Abbas), Anugerah Pertubuhan Bukan Kerajaan (NGO), and Tokoh Imam, Bilal dan Siak award (Anugerah Pegawai Masjid).

Title: Ayob Khan: Tokoh Wira Negara Award honours sacrifices of police personnel
Article:
SERDANG: For Tan Sri Ayob Khan Mydin Pitchay, the national-level Maulidur Rasul Tokoh Wira Negara Award recognises not only his service but also the sacrifices of police personnel in protecting the country.
The newly-retired deputy inspector-general of police said he was caught by surprise, having only been informed of his selection last Friday.
"Indeed, I did not expect to be chosen to receive the National-level Maulidur Rasul Tokoh Wira Negara Award. I was only informed last Friday afternoon.
"This award is not just a recognition for me, but also for the police," he told reporters after the award ceremony here today.
Ayob expressed his appreciation to the government and the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (Jakim) for choosing him to receive the award.
Reflecting on his career, Ayob said he had made numerous arrests of terrorists in the line of duty, although he had never engaged in direct combat with them.
"I have never fought the communists or terrorists. I only made arrests," he said.
Now retired, Ayob said he had yet to decide on his next move despite receiving several offers including from government-linked companies and the corporate sector.
He said he was considering opportunities with non-governmental organisations, the corporate sector or writing, which he has a keen interest in.
"I believe I need to be active again, whether in an NGO, companies or writing," he said.
Having previously published 'Dari Pendang ke Bukit Aman, Ayob said he was also considering writing a more detailed account of his past operations to share with the public.
Ayob also confirmed receiving offers from political parties, but said he had yet to make a decision.
"I am still studying and considering them," he said.
Ayob was named Tokoh Wira Negara for his contributions to national security and efforts to combat terrorism and organised crime.
He previously headed the Bukit Aman Special Branch Counter-Terrorism Division (E8), Johor police and the Narcotics Crime Investigation Department.
During his career, he was involved in efforts to disrupt terrorist cells and international and domestic militant networks, as well as operations against organised crime and drug trafficking.

Title: Singapore checkpoint bust: Malaysian man held, 700 cartons seized
Article:
SINGAPORE: A 30-year-old Malaysian man was arrested after Singapore authorities found more than 700 cartons and 100 packets of duty-unpaid cigarettes hidden in his car at the Woodlands Checkpoint.
Singapore's Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA) said in a social media post that its officers directed the Malaysian-registered vehicle for enhanced checks on Aug 10.
The contraband items were found hidden in modified compartments throughout the vehicle.
The suspect and the seized cigarettes were handed over to Singapore Customs for further investigation.
Possessing, buying, selling, or dealing in duty-unpaid goods are serious offences under Singapore law, punishable by heavy fines, imprisonment, or both.
The arrest follows another
smuggling attempt
at the same checkpoint earlier this month, where officers found over 600 cartons and 900 packets of duty-unpaid cigarettes hidden in the floorboard of a Malaysian-registered vehicle.
The 26-year-old Malaysian driver in that case was also arrested.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pakistan and Iran made 'significant progress' in talks on conflict, minister says
Article:
ISLAMABAD: Pakistan and Iran made "significant progress" in talks that focused on the US-Israeli war on Iran and a path to peace, Pakistan's interior minister said on Tuesday, at the end of a visit to Teheran.
Talks between the two sides focused on measures to prevent further escalation, reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and an expedited termination of the conflict, a statement from the Pakistani military said about the meeting between the country's army chief, Asim Munir, and the Iranian leadership.
The two sides also exchanged views on regional peace and the way to arrive at a negotiated settlement to the dispute, the statement said.
"The Iranian President candidly shared his government's perspective and we had a very constructive exchange on the issues involved," Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, who accompanied Munir to Teheran, said in a post on X.
The White House and the State Department did not immediately respond to requests for comment made outside business hours.
Munir spoke with US President Donald Trump ahead of his Teheran visit, Reuters reported on Monday.
Trump last week warned of economic consequences against any country that provided "any type of lifeline to Iran" as he seeks to isolate the country.
Iran in turn vowed ‌to shut down all oil exports from the Gulf.

Title: PM: Maulidur Rasul a time to practise Prophet Muhammad's teachings
Article:
SERDANG: Maulidur Rasul should not be viewed merely as a celebration but as a chance for Muslims to appreciate and apply the teachings of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) in their daily lives.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the true significance of commemorating the Prophet's birth lay in how his teachings and values were reflected in the conduct of Muslims and their contribution to society.
"The challenge for the ummah is appreciation," he said at the national-level Maulidur Rasul celebration.
Anwar said Muslims should strive to become exemplary not only among fellow Muslims but also to humanity as a whole, in line with the message of rahmat lil alamin (mercy to all creation).
He said this required Muslims to demonstrate good values, respect, justice and excellence in their daily lives rather than merely displaying their faith through outward activities.
"Islam is not just about displaying or rebuking, but about attracting others through the best example," he said.
He said every Muslim had a role to play in demonstrating these values, whether as a government leader, minister, academic or student.
"If you are a leader, lead well. If you are a professor, be a good professor. Students can do so too. Ministers must also be prepared to bring change and deliver a clear message."
Anwar said the life of Prophet Muhammad provided lessons for Muslims to embrace social transformation, continuously improve themselves, and strive towards becoming an exemplary community grounded in the Quran, good character and strong values.
Meanwhile, Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan urged Malaysians to reject hatred, insults and provocation despite differences in political views, race and social background.
Drawing on the Prophet's teachings on peaceful coexistence, he said the concept of At-Ta'ayush, or living together harmoniously, was particularly important in Malaysia's multiracial and multireligious society.
Zulkifli said love for the Prophet Muhammad should be reflected through actions that promoted peace and strengthened relations between communities, rather than creating division.
"In a diverse society, every citizen has a responsibility to preserve harmony and reject hate speech and provocation that could damage relations between communities."

Title: Washington Post ordered to rehire fired columnist
Article:
WASHINGTON: The Washington Post was ordered Monday to reinstate columnist Karen Attiah, who was fired over social media posts she wrote in the aftermath of right-wing influencer Charlie Kirk's assassination.
Kirk was shot dead in September on a Utah college campus, sparking a wave of grief among conservatives and threats of a clampdown on the "radical left" from President Donald Trump.
Attiah wrote on social media afterward that she would not display sadness for Kirk's killing and shared the activist's past racist comments about Black women.
She was later fired, with the Post accusing her of "gross misconduct" and of violating its social media policies, according to the paper's own reporting.
An arbitrator ordered the Post on Monday to rehire Attiah and compensate her with back pay, writing in the decision that the Post "did not have good and sufficient cause" for her dismissal.
Attiah wrote on X that she was "happy" at the decision, saying she had been forced out for "speaking the truth."
The Post said it respected the arbitration process but declined to comment further.
Attiah had worked at the publication for 11 years and noted that she was the "last remaining Black full-time opinion columnist at the Post" at the time of her firing.
In her posts about Kirk, she shared his racist claims that Black women lack "brain processing power" and therefore require help from diversity programmes.
Her other posts took aim at the Trump administration's framing of Kirk as a martyr for the conservative cause.
Since 2013, when billionaire Amazon founder Jeff Bezos purchased the Post, the newspaper's opinion section has shifted its tone to focus more on "personal liberties and free markets," according to internal mandates.
Attiah gained recognition as the editor for journalist Jamal Khashoggi, a Saudi national with US residency who was murdered in the Saudi consulate in Istanbul in 2018.
US intelligence and a United Nations investigation later concluded that Riyadh bore responsibility for his killing.
Attiah had recruited Khashoggi to write about the Arab world, and published his posthumous last column, which called for free expression in the region.
She has advocated for human rights and free expression in her work ever since.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Thailand car production rises 6.1pct on year in July
Article:
BANGKOK: Car production in Thailand rose 6.12 per cent in July from a year earlier to 117,383 units, the Federation of Thai Industries (FTI) said on Tuesday.
The reading follows a year-on-year fall of 7.55 per cent in June. The FTI has previously forecast a 3.33 per cent drop in car production for the whole of 2026.
July domestic car sales rose 20.07 per cent versus a rise of 17.26 per cent in June, the federation said.
Exports in July rose 2.39 per cent compared to a drop of 7.45 per cent in the previous month, according to the FTI.
Thailand is Southeast Asia's biggest auto production centre and an export base for some of the world's leading carmakers, including Toyota and Honda.

Title: 'We're going to keep going': Venezuelan quake rescuers soldier on
Article:
TWO months after two huge earthquakes struck Venezuela and killed thousands, volunteer rescuer Domingo Pacheco still faces a mountain of work.
The 53-year-old reached the worst-hit coastal state of La Guaira in the immediate aftermath of the quakes and has been picking through the rubble ever since.
The magnitude 7.2 and 7.5 tremors hit within a minute of each other on June 24, killing over 6,500 people.
Pacheco has the unenviable task of looking for an unknown number of lifeless victims still buried under the debris, although he avoids thinking about the emotional impact.
The work is physically challenging, too.
One evening, after one of many exhausting days of digging through the detritus, he lost his breath and blacked out for a few seconds.
"The oxygen was slowly taken away from me until I kind of lost consciousness," Pacheco told AFP.
"Everything went blurry and I thought of my young son before asking myself, 'What's going on?'"
When the volunteer arrived in June, he went straight to work, searching for a little girl buried under a collapsed social housing complex.
He recalls a trapped family who had lived on the top floor, begging to be rescued during those first hours of confusion.
"There were people screaming, asking us to help them," he said. "I went where I was needed."
Pacheco volunteers with the Unified Rescue Group of Venezuela (GRUV), which depends on donations and has rescued 21 people alive and recovered 56 bodies.
Witnessing the determination of families who refuse to give up on loved ones still trapped under the impenetrable rubble has "profoundly impacted" him, he told AFP.
[[nid:1518399]]
There are no official figures to show how many people remain missing after the quakes.
"When to close this chapter?" Pacheco asked.
"God willing, as soon as possible, so that everyone, so that those family members too, can find relief from the suffering they are going through, from not being able to recover their loved ones."
Frank Viloria met Pacheco and his GRUV colleagues in Playa Grande, where entire residential complexes crumbled against a backdrop of stunning sea views.
Viloria's sister and niece died when their eight-story building fell to pieces.
"When I see him, I'm happy," he said with a smile, shaking hands with Pacheco, who calls him "son."
"I'm very grateful to them. I feel a lot of respect and admiration; I can vouch for them because I saw how they work," the 38-year-old added.
The men hug when they say goodbye.
Located north of Caracas, La Guaira is usually a favourite weekend getaway spot for residents of the capital.
Its once touristy atmosphere has been replaced by tragedy these past few months, and thousands of people made homeless by the quakes now live in makeshift camps under difficult conditions.
"Sometimes I'm very sad; my mind is here...it's never at home" in Caracas, said Pacheco.
"We're going to keep going for as long as the body allows," he said.
* The writer is from AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'Militants tracked my jogging routine' - Ayob Khan
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Being constantly on guard became second nature to former deputy inspector-general of police Tan Sri Ayob Khan Mydin Pitchay, particularly during his years at the forefront of the country's fight against terrorism.
He knew there were eyes watching him, even when he went jogging at Taman Tasik Perdana.
Ayob revealed that Islamic State-linked militants had recruited Malaysians through social media to monitor security personnel, including tracking the movements and routines of senior police officers.
"They tracked the movements of certain officers, including the inspector-general of police at the time. They knew I would go for a jog at Taman Tasik Perdana, and that then IGP (Tan Sri Khalid Abu Bakar) went for convoy bike rides on Saturdays.
"I received information about this because we were also in the group (monitoring them)," Ayob was quoted as saying in an interview with Free Malaysia Today (FMT).
Ayob, who recently retired after 35 years in the police force, headed Bukit Aman's counter-terrorism division from 2016 to 2020, where he became known for dismantling militant cells and thwarting terror plots.
This meant he had to take additional security precautions, including travelling in a bulletproof vehicle, frequently changing routes and remaining constantly alert with his surroundings.
Even while eating at restaurants, Ayob said he would sit facing outwards so he could monitor the movements of those around him.
He said such security practices were rooted in techniques developed during the country's fight against the Malayan Communist Party from the 1950s to the 1980s.
Ayob also defended the need for specialised legal tools such as the Security Offences (Special Measures) Act 2012 (Sosma) as he said the law remained important in tackling serious security threats, particularly terrorism and organised crime.
However, he said, he was not advocating for the return of the Internal Security Act 1960 (ISA), which allowed detention without trial.
The ISA was repealed in 2012 and replaced by Sosma, which allows suspects to be detained for up to 28 days for investigations before they must either be charged or released.
Ayob said conventional remand procedures under general criminal law were inadequate when investigators were dealing with major terrorism operations involving numerous suspects.
"I didn't just arrest one person when I was in counter-terrorism. Within 24 hours, I arrested 40 suspects," he was quoted as saying.
He said investigators needed sufficient time to examine seized items, analyse mobile phones and laptops, and complete investigations involving dozens of individuals, something that would be difficult if courts granted only short remand periods.
Ayob said security laws were also necessary to prevent communal tensions from escalating in Malaysia's multiracial society, citing previous racial clashes in Kampung Medan and Kampung Rawa.
"Our social fabric is different. We cannot simply take the model Western countries use," he said.
He cautioned politicians against viewing security legislation through the lens of short-term political mileage, saying the country's long-term safety had to take precedence.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Social media, popular culture threatening Muslim identity, says Sultan Nazrin
Article:
IPOH: Social media, popular culture, entertainment and global lifestyles are increasingly shaping the minds of younger generations and posing serious challenges to Muslim character and the identity of the ummah.
Sultan of Perak Sultan Nazrin Muizzuddin Shah said Muslims must strike a careful balance between embracing modernity and preserving their religious principles and identity.
He said thoughtful efforts were needed to ensure modern influences did not erode Muslim values or create a crisis of confidence in their own identity.
"Against this backdrop, both Muslim character and the identity of the ummah face serious challenges that must be addressed. Muslims are increasingly exposed to global influences.
"Social media, popular culture, entertainment and global lifestyles are shaping the minds of the younger generation," he said.
Sultan Nazrin said this at the state-level Maulidur Rasul celebration themed "Fostering Muslim Character – Fortifying the Identity of the Ummah".
Also present were Raja Permaisuri Perak Tuanku Zara Salim, Raja Muda of Perak Raja Jaafar Raja Muda Musa, Raja Di-Hilir Perak Raja Iskandar Dzulkarnain Sultan Idris and Perak Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad.
Sultan Nazrin said the Muslim community was also facing increasingly serious challenges to its unity.
"Differences in politics, schools of Islamic thought, race and interests, together with the pursuit of influence, rank, position, wealth and worldly luxury, are increasingly outweighing the spirit of brotherhood, causing that sense of brotherhood to become progressively marginalised," he said.
He also called on Muslim leaders, Islamic organisations and movements to avoid unnecessary disputes and minimise political rivalry.
"Greater priority should be given to initiatives that can strengthen and elevate the identity of the Muslim community.
"It is encouraging, and something for which we should be grateful, that while political leaders and factions choose to compete and be in conflict, there are also individuals and groups pioneering positive initiatives and advancing awareness in Islamic education, Islamic economy, Islamic finance, halal industries, Islamic endowments, digital Islamic outreach and the strengthening of the family institution.
"These positive efforts must be expanded, strengthened and brought to fruition," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tighter Iran curbs could raise risks for Malaysian firms
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia could face some financial and trade-related risks if ship-to-ship transfers involving sanctioned Iranian oil continue off its waters, economists said.
The risks will be more likely to affect specific Malaysian companies and intermediaries than the country as a whole, particularly if they are found to have facilitated transactions that breach US sanctions.
The US has repeatedly warned of severe economic penalties on countries that assist or do business with Iran, they added.
UniKL Business School economic analyst Associate Professor Dr Aimi Zulhazmi Abdul Rashid said Malaysian shipping companies, ports, insurers and banks that facilitate these sales of Iranian oil could face secondary sanctions such as frozen US assets and cut off from its financial system.
"Reports have flagged ship-to-ship transfers of Iranian oil in international waters off Malaysia as part of Iran's 'dark fleet' operations.
"If the US decides to escalate enforcement, Malaysia as a country is unlikely to be sanctioned wholesale, but specific entities or individuals could be. That would hurt Malaysia's reputation as a neutral trading hub,"  he told Business Times.
Washington will announce new strategies that will intensify its conflict with Iran which is now in its sixth month.
In an op-ed published on Sunday, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned of a "D-Day" that is coming for Iran, ahead of a scheduled press conference later today.
Bessent called it "the single greatest financial offensive ever marshalled against an adversary".
US President Donald Trump previously said he was launching a major new campaign to target Iran's economy, threatening "tremendous" punishment on any country that helps or does business with the Islamic republic.
Aimi said intensified war between the two countries could also increase fuel and food costs, while disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz could result in higher insurance and a rise in freight costs for Malaysia's palm oil and liquified natural gas exports.
"Malaysia's official stance has been to comply with UN sanctions, but enforcement at sea is difficult. If the Trump administration pushes harder, Putrajaya will be under pressure to crack down publicly," he added.
Putra Business School MBA programme director Prof Dr Ahmed Razman Abdul Latiff said Malaysia could face indirect economic and financial risks, particularly if its companies, ports, shipping operators, financial institutions or other intermediaries are found to be knowingly involved in transactions designed to circumvent US sanctions.
"For Malaysia, the immediate concern would be reputational and financial rather than necessarily direct sanctions against the entire country.
"Any company linked to sanctioned Iranian oil could potentially face restrictions on access to the US financial system, banking transactions, insurance or international trade.
"Therefore, Malaysian authorities and businesses need to strengthen monitoring and enforcement, particularly involving suspicious ship-to-ship transfers and opaque trading activities in Malaysian waters," he added.
Earlier this month, US trade regulators flagged Malaysia among more than 40 trade partners identified as risks for aiding tariff evasion, as Washington intensifies its global crackdown on China-linked transshipment networks.
In a report titled 'The Great Transshipment Scam: Rise, Scope, and Costs,' the White House Office of Trade and Manufacturing Policy named Malaysia alongside more than 40 countries accused of serving as conduits for illegal pass-through trade.
OIL PRICES TO RE-TEST US$100 LEVELS
Razman said crude oil prices will hit US$100 per barrel again if the conflict leads to further disruptions. "The main concern is not simply the war itself, but whether oil production, tanker movements and supply routes are seriously affected."
However, he said prices may stabilise if there is a diplomatic breakthrough or alternative supplies from other producers can offset the disruption.
Oil prices have risen more than US$100 per barrel since the war took place, surging to US$126.41 per barrel on April 30 driven by severe supply disruptions at the Strait of Hormuz.
Nusantara Academy for Strategic Research senior fellow Dr Azmi Hassan said Malaysia will be "penalised" for practicing its sovereignty to trade with other countries.
"US sanction on Iran is unilateral and that is why Malaysia does not recognise this particular sanction. If the sanction was by the United Nations then it'll be a different story," he said.
Additionally, Aimi said Brent prices have reached US$100 during the flare ups.
"For Malaysia, the immediate hit is inflation, but the bigger risk is being caught in US secondary sanctions over Iranian oil trade. The longer Hormuz stays risky, the more persistent the energy inflation shock will be," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sultan Nazrin: True love for Prophet Muhammad means living by his teachings
Article:
IPOH: The commemoration of Prophet Muhammad's (pbuh) birth should extend beyond religious ceremonies, serving as a reminder for Muslims to reflect on how deeply his teachings shape their character and way of life.
Sultan of Perak Sultan Nazrin Muizzuddin Shah said the true measure of love for the Prophet was reflected not in words or ceremonies, but in how far his teachings, character and practices influenced daily conduct.
"We may send blessings upon him. We may gather in assemblies of religious learning or take part in processions commemorating his birth. We may speak about his life and his mission.
"Yet the true measure of our love for Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) lies not in words or ceremonies, but in the extent to which his teachings, character and practices shape our conduct and contribute to the strength of the Muslim community," he said.
Sultan Nazrin said in his speech at the state-level Maulidur Rasul celebration, themed "Fostering Muslim Character – Fortifying the Identity of the Ummah".
Also present were Raja Permaisuri Perak Tuanku Zara Salim, Raja Muda Perak Raja Jaafar Raja Muda Musa, Raja Di-Hilir Perak Raja Iskandar Dzulkarnain Sultan Idris and Perak Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad.
Sultan Nazrin said a strong Muslim character must originate from within.
"It encompasses the identity, character and principles of life of a Muslim, founded upon faith, Islamic law, piety, knowledge and noble character.
"These values are reflected in one's thoughts, speech, actions and way of life. Such a person understands the purpose of life, stands firm on fundamental principles, and does not easily lose direction even in an ever-changing world," he said.
Sultan Nazrin said the identity of the Muslim community was no longer uniform.
"Muslims live in different countries, cultures and political systems, and the community is confronted by many influences arising from the changing times.
"Although religious identity remains strong, the extent to which Islam is understood and practised increasingly varies.
"For some Muslims, Islam is inherited by birth alone, without genuine understanding or without truly embracing the faith.
"Thus, although Islam remains a source of guidance, among some segments of the Muslim community it is increasingly expressed through symbols and rituals, while fundamental Islamic principles and values such as trustworthiness, honesty, justice, noble character, discipline, knowledge, modesty and benevolence are becoming less evident in everyday life," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Cybersecurity must go hand in hand with cyber resilience
Article:
LETTER:
FOR years, our approach to digital vulnerability has been straightforward: secure the perimeter, authenticate users, encrypt data and pass compliance audits.
Yet incidents continue to occur, not necessarily because security measures are inadequate but because we often confuse cybersecurity with cyber resilience.
An organisation can hold multiple certifications and implement extensive security controls yet still suffer serious disruption when a critical system or dependency goes offline.
Estonia offered an early warning. In 2007, a sustained cyberattack disrupted government, banking and media services, demonstrating how digital dependence can turn a cyber incident into a disruption of essential societal functions.
Each organisation may appear secure within its own domain while its ability to function depends on external systems beyond its control.
A failure at one point in the ecosystem can therefore propagate across organisations and sectors.
Cyber resilience means designing systems and institutions to continue functioning despite any disruption.
Malaysia has strengthened its cybersecurity legislation, institutions and regulatory frameworks, providing an essential foundation.
But compliance frameworks primarily ask whether required controls are in place.
They do not, by themselves, answer the question that resilience demands: what happens when those controls fail, a supplier goes offline or a critical service becomes unavailable?
This matters as our country becomes increasingly dependent on interconnected and digitalised critical infrastructure across government, healthcare, finance, transportation, energy and other essential services.
Thus, we must ensure that failure in one system does not become failure across an entire ecosystem.
When the next major disruption occurs, whether caused by a cyber attack, human error, software failure or technical breakdown, will hospitals continue treating patients? Will airports continue processing passengers? Will banks continue moving money? Will government agencies remain able to reach citizens?
These are not merely cybersecurity questions. They are questions of societal resilience. The next stage of digital development must therefore be resilience by design.
PROFESSOR DR SELVAKUMAR MANICKAM
Director,
Cybersecurity Research Centre,
Universiti Sains Malaysia

Title: Six months of war: 20 dead in 68 incidents near Hormuz, IMO says
Article:
LONDON: The Strait of Hormuz has been the main focus of the six-month war between Iran and the US and Israel, with many commercial vessels targeted in the vital conduit for oil and gas shipments.
In total, 68 incidents have been confirmed by the International Maritime Organisation (IMO) in the Gulf and neighbouring bodies of water, the equivalent of one every 2.6 days.
Across all incidents, at least 20 seafarers or port workers were reported killed, 35 wounded and one missing, the UN maritime agency said.
About half of the incidents have involved tankers, 20 per cent container ships and 15 per cent bulk carriers.
The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) classified 47 of the incidents as attacks.
Liberia-flagged vessels have been most affected, being involved in 13 incidents, followed by 10 vessels each from Panama and the Marshall Islands.
Iran-flagged vessels were reported as being involved in four incidents.
The rate of incidents has ebbed and flowed during the various phases of the war.
From the outbreak of war at the end of February until an agreement establishing a framework for peace talks was struck in mid-June, an incident was reported on average once every 2.3 days.
Incidents during this period accounted for 16 of the deaths and 19 of the injuries, and were recorded throughout the Gulf – both east and west of Hormuz, and off the coasts of Iraq, Iran, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Oman and the United Arab Emirates.
As peace talks continued, until around July 7, that rate halved to one incident every 4.6 days, on average.
No seafarers or other workers were reported killed, missing or injured during this period.
Four of the five incidents during this period were clustered off the Omani coast around the strait's narrowest point, along a route not authorised by Iranian authorities.
Iran, which hopes to retain control of the Hormuz after the war and charge fees for passage, had warned vessels against taking the alternative route.
Since talks collapsed, the rate has climbed almost back to pre-talks levels, with an incident recorded on average every 2.8 days.
Four seafarers or workers have been killed, 16 injured and one reported missing as a result.

Title: Penang Hindu Endowments Board urged to clarify temple demolition notice
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Former Penang Hindu Endowments Board (PHEB) commissioner and Urimai secretary-general Satees Muniandy has urged the board to clarify why the Seberang Prai City Council issued a demolition notice to a Hindu temple in Batu Kawan.
Satees said the temple was among 10 places of worship relocated to land owned by PHEB during his tenure in the Penang state government.
He said the city council had the right to issue such a notice if the land was illegally occupied or the building stood on private land.
"However, the said temple is on PHEB's land and the city council has no business issuing the notice," he said today.
Satees said the present PHEB management should explain the temple's status, including whether ownership of the land had been transferred to another party since the previous board members left in 2023.
He added that, in matters involving the relocation of Hindu temples, the city council should also have contacted the Penang Development Corporation to obtain a clearer picture of the temple's status.
"Rather than responding unilaterally to the Hindu temple in Batu Kawan, the city council should have consulted the PHEB on the matter," he added.
PHEB manages Hindu religious endowments, including temple land and property, in the state.
The New Straits Times has reached out to Seberang Prai City Council mayor Datuk Baderul Amin Abdul Hamid for comment.

Title: Pengerang peat fire still burning across area the size of 51 football fields
Article:
KOTA TINGGI: Firefighters continue to battle a peat fire the size of 51 football fields along the Sebana Cove-Punggai Bypass road in Pengerang, with round-the-clock operations ongoing.
About 15ha of the 51.4ha area has been extinguished, while the fire continues to burn across some 36.4ha.
Johor Fire and Rescue Department operations commander Baharuddin Idris said firemen had been working continuously to put out the flames since yesterday.
However, firefighters faced several challenges, including difficult terrain, strong winds, limited water supply and hot, dry weather, which further complicated containment efforts.
A total of 21 personnel are at the scene, including four Civil Defence Force members and an excavator operator.
No casualties or injuries were reported, and no new flames were detected during the latest assessment, Baharuddin said in a statement.

working together

Title: [UPDATED] Anwar: Felda forensic audit proposal to be brought to cabinet [WATCH]
Article:
SERDANG: The proposal for a forensic audit into alleged wrongdoing involving the Federal Land Development Authority (Felda) will be brought to the cabinet for discussion.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said this when met by reporters after the national-level Maulidur Rasul celebration today.
"We will bring it for discussion at the cabinet," he said.
Earlier, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi called for a forensic audit of Felda, saying any suspected abuse of power, breach of trust or governance failures must be
thoroughly investigated
.
He said those responsible for any wrongdoing should be brought to court if there was strong evidence against them, but cautioned against using investigations to humiliate individuals.
Anwar had previously said Felda was burdened with nearly RM10 billion in debts and losses following years of management failures and excessive political interference.
He said Felda had once been among the world's largest plantation organisations and generated billions of ringgit in annual profits before its financial position deteriorated.
The government is now paying RM980 million annually to meet Felda's financial obligations arising from losses incurred under its previous management/
On Friday, Anwar said a special task force tasked with investigating Felda's management had begun work, adding that he would await its full findings before making an official announcement.
He said the task force would
examine Felda's past problems
, current management and future direction, with its findings to be made public upon completion.

Title: Immigration lodges police report over viral UTC Pudu passport cover incident
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Immigration Department has lodged a police report over a viral social media post by a woman who claimed she was humiliated and accused of stealing a passport cover at the UTC Pudu Immigration office.
The woman had alleged that the incident occurred while she was applying for a passport.
Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said the department had reviewed closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage, relevant records and statements from officers on duty following the allegations.
He said the review found that several claims made in the viral post were inconsistent with the CCTV footage, records and accounts obtained from officers.
"The department views this matter seriously to ensure that the actual circumstances can be clarified based on the facts obtained.
"Therefore, a police report has been lodged for further action and the department will give its full cooperation," he said in a statement today.
The controversy stemmed from a social media post recounting the woman's experience at the UTC Pudu Immigration office on Aug 21.
In the post, she claimed that she had accidentally taken a passport cover after believing it had been provided with her newly issued passport.
She said while waiting for her husband, she was then called by Immigration officers and taken to a room, where she was surrounded by more than 10 officers.
The woman alleged that she was shouted at and accused of stealing the passport cover despite attempting to explain that she had taken it by mistake.
She also claimed that her husband was reprimanded when he attempted to defend her and that they were asked to produce their mobile phones so officers could check their call logs following a dispute over an alleged telephone call made by the officers.
According to her account, officers later discovered that the wrong telephone number had been called.
The woman further alleged that she was given the choice of being taken to a police station or writing a statement admitting that she had stolen the passport cover.
She said she eventually wrote a statement saying she had "accidentally taken" the cover, rather than stolen it, maintaining that she had no intention to steal.
She said the passport cover was subsequently returned and that she remained at the premises throughout the incident while waiting for her husband.
The woman also said she had lodged a complaint with the Home Ministry over the way the matter was handled.
Zakaria said the department respected individuals' right to express their views, share their experiences or lodge complaints about its services.
However he said the information shared should be accurate and comprehensive to allow matters to be assessed fairly and prevent misunderstandings.
He said the department remained committed to handling complaints transparently, professionally and without prejudice, while providing services with integrity and in the public interest.

Title: Land, building issues among main causes of strata title delays
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Issues involving land, buildings, applicants and documentation have been identified as the four main reasons strata homeowners may wait years, in some cases more than two decades, to obtain their strata titles.
Federal Department of Lands and Mines (Strata and Stratum Titles Division) director Danial Lee Abdullah said some homeowners viewed the lack of a strata title as a non-issue as long as they could continue living in their properties.
"Some residents have lived there for decades and grown complacent without a grant or title. They feel that even without ownership documents, they can still live there without any issue.
"It is only when they attempt a transaction requiring official approval that they suddenly realise the need for a title deed," he told Bernama.
Danial Lee said land issues could arise when structures were built across multiple lots, requiring lot amalgamation before titles could be issued.
Building-related delays often stemmed from missing or untraceable original plans, forcing authorities to draw up replacement blueprints based on existing structures, he added.
"This is not a process that can be resolved in a day or two, as it requires approvals from state government authorities," he said.
Applicant-related complications could arise when landowners died or developer companies were wound up, became untraceable or faced financial difficulties, he said.
Incomplete documentation, including missing approved building plans, could further delay applications.
He highlighted the fundamental legal distinction between titles and contracts, noting that while a sale and purchase agreement is simply a private contract with a developer, a strata title guarantees state-recognised property ownership.
"The absence of strata titles also impacts scheme management, because title registration triggers the establishment of a management corporation (MC) responsible for common property, maintenance, and security services," he said.
Danial Lee said state Land and Mines Offices were empowered to take legal action against landowners who failed to apply for strata titles.
Penalties include fines of between RM10,000 and RM100,000, a prison sentence of up to three years, or both, with additional daily fines of RM100 to RM1,000 for ongoing non-compliance.
He advised homeowners who had yet to secure their strata titles to request status updates from their developers or Joint Management Bodies, and to escalate the matter to state Land and Mines Offices if developers failed to comply.
Danial Lee said process improvements had also been made to the issuance of strata titles under Federal Director General of Land and Mines Circular No. 9/2026, which sets a 100-day target for title issuance, effective Aug 18. — BERNAMA

Title: [UPDATED]: Syed Azman named Tokoh Perdana Maulidur Rasul, Ayob Khan also honoured
Article:
SERDANG: Weststar Group founder and managing director Tan Sri Dr Syed Azman Syed Ibrahim has been named the recipient of the 2026 national-level Tokoh Perdana Maulidur Rasul award.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim presented the award to Syed Azman at the National Maulidur Rasul celebration today.
Former deputy Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Ayob Khan Mydin Pitchay was named Tokoh Wira Negara for his contributions to national security and efforts in combating terrorism and organised crime.
Others honoured included Islamic scholar Maulana Abdul Hamid Chin (Tokoh Agamawan), International Islamic University Malaysia (IIUM) Professor Dr Ruzita Mohd Amin (Tokoh Wanita Madani), and former Malaysian Palm Oil Board (MPOB) director-general Datuk Dr Ahmad Parveez Ghulam Kadir (Tokoh Saintis).
Angkatan Belia Islam Malaysia (Abim) president Ahmad Fahmi Mohd Samsudin was named Tokoh Belia Harapan, while Laman Yasim from Sarawak received the Tokoh Keluarga Mithali award.
Muhammad Mikhael Sathayah, better known as social media personality "Muka Gangster", was recognised as Tokoh Khas (Saudara Baru Cemerlang).
Syed Azman, 66, is the founder and managing director of Weststar Group, which has grown into a major player in the helicopter services industry, particularly in supporting the oil and gas sector.
He began his career in the Malaysian Armed Forces in 1981 after completing his schooling and joined the Royal Intelligence Corps before serving with the Defence Intelligence Staff Division.
He later ventured into the private sector and built Weststar into a diversified business group, with Weststar Aviation Services emerging as a major provider of helicopter services to the oil and gas industry.
The company operates more than 40 helicopters and has provided services to major oil and gas companies, including Petronas Carigali, Shell and Tullow Oil.
Beyond business, Syed Azman has been involved in various philanthropic and community initiatives, including supporting mosque and surau development, disaster relief, orphanages and welfare programmes.
He has also supported welfare initiatives for Malaysian Armed Forces veterans and their families.
In September 2025, he was appointed chairman of the board of Universiti Pertahanan Nasional Malaysia (UPNM).

Title: One-third seats could boost Sabah, Sarawak's federal leverage
Article:
PETALING JAYA: Allocating one-third of parliamentary seats to Sabah and Sarawak could give the two states significantly greater influence over the formation of the federal government, analysts said.
Political analyst Awang Azman Pawi said if Sabah and Sarawak held 78 seats, or roughly one-third of the current 222-seat Dewan Rakyat, the two states would need the support of just 34 MPs from the peninsula to reach the 112 seats required for a simple majority.
Conversely, a Peninsular coalition seeking to govern without the support of Sabah and Sarawak would need to win 112 of the remaining 144 seats, or nearly 78 per cent.
That would be a considerably higher hurdle than at present, when Peninsular Malaysia holds 166 seats and a coalition would need about 67 per cent of them to reach the 112-seat threshold on its own.
"The mathematics is revealing," Awang Azman said.
Sabah and Sarawak are currently allocated 56 of the 222 Dewan Rakyat seats, or about a quarter of the House.
Calls for the two states to be allocated one-third of parliamentary seats have gained renewed attention amid concerns that greater cooperation among Peninsular parties could allow a future government to be formed without relying heavily on East Malaysian support.
Last week, SUPP Youth vice-chairman Kelvin Hii cited an Ilham Centre projection suggesting that a BN-PN alliance could win up to 122 parliamentary seats in the peninsula at the next general election.
Hii said the projection showed why Sabah and Sarawak needed one-third representation, warning that the two states should not be put in a position where they could be disregarded simply because their support was no longer needed to form the federal government.
James Chin of the University of Tasmania said an Umno-Pas combination could become a powerful electoral force in the peninsula.
Based on his own calculations, Chin said the two parties could potentially win up to 105 seats if they were able to remain together until the next general election, although they would still fall short of the 112 needed to govern alone.
"If Pas and Umno can hold together and stay as allies until the next general election, we will have the Malay tsunami," he said.
Awang Azman added that the prospect of greater electoral cooperation among Peninsular parties was becoming more realistic, even if a permanent grand coalition remained unlikely.
"BN and PN do not need perfect ideological unity to diminish Sabah and Sarawak's leverage," he said.
Effective seat negotiations, fewer multi-cornered contests and sufficient transfer of votes in Malay-majority constituencies could be enough to significantly improve their electoral performance.
"East Malaysian leaders have recognised that their present leverage is contingent on Peninsular fragmentation," Awang Azman said.
"If BN-PN or any future Peninsular alignment can obtain 112 seats independently, that leverage disappears."
POWER DEPENDS ON UNITY
However, Awang Azman cautioned against treating the 78 East Malaysian seats as a single political bloc.
Sabah and Sarawak parties have different interests, while national parties also contest and win seats in both states. Sabah politics, in particular, remains highly fragmented.
"Their bargaining power becomes exceptional only if they can coordinate around common federal issues such as MA63, fiscal powers, development allocations, petroleum rights and constitutional amendments."
There is also an important caveat to the 78-seat calculation: it assumes the Dewan Rakyat remains at 222 seats.
However, Chin said the Electoral Commission assesses the redrawing of boundaries for the whole of Malaysia every eight years to account for population increases and other changes.
"If you're going to increase the seats for Sabah and Sarawak, then for certain states in Peninsular Malaysia, you also have to increase their seats," Chin added.
If additional Sabah and Sarawak seats are created without reducing Peninsular representation, the total size of Parliament would increase, along with the thresholds needed for both a simple and two-thirds majority.
According to Awang Azman, the eventual balance of power would therefore depend not just on how many additional seats Sabah and Sarawak receive, but also on the final size and composition of the Dewan Rakyat.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 350 EV charging points planned for major highways by 2028
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 350 electric vehicle (EV) charging points will be installed across the North-South Expressway and East Coast Expressway 2 networks by 2028.
PLUS Malaysia Berhad transport development head Datuk Nik Airina Nik Jaffar told Berita Harian that the commitment would strengthen the low-carbon mobility ecosystem in line with Phase I of the Low Carbon Mobility Development Plan.
"Under Phase II of the plan, 118 EV charging points across strategic locations are already operational, including at rest and service areas along the highways.
"This is an initiative under the Low Carbon Mobility Development Plan (2021-2030), which supports the Green Highway Traffic Plan 2.0," she told Berita Harian.
She said the project was carried out in collaboration with the government and appointed operators, including JomCharge, Gentari Go and ChargeEV, to meet current and future EV charging demand while reducing congestion at certain locations.
"We are not only expanding coverage, but are also strategising the placement of Direct Current fast-charging points, the first of their kind on Malaysian highways, which are expected to be fully ready by 2027.
"We are targeting 20 to 30 EV charging points at strategic locations along traffic corridors, particularly those with high potential for congestion during peak times," she said.
She said that under the government's directive, PLUS is planning to introduce Dynamic Fast Charging Under Contingency technology, with an output capacity of between 47 kilowatts (kW) and 200kW by 2026.
Meanwhile, a check by Berita Harian at several locations along the PLUS highway and Seremban-Port Dickson Highway found EV charging facilities at many main rest and service areas.
Mohd Rizal Mohd Rais, 44, said EV charging points should be provided at all main rest and service areas as some drivers were worried about running out of battery during peak periods.
He also hoped more facilities would be provided at strategic locations.
Charging point operators such as Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB) provide facilities in stages according to petrol station capacity, although not all petrol stations at rest and service areas have EV charging points due to lower demand.
Motorcyclist Mohd Nizam Zainal said the increase in EV ownership required more charging stations.
EV user Azliya Ghazali, 52, said she still faced charging issues after becoming an EV owner in February.
"I plan my journeys in advance based on distance and my vehicle's battery level, so I don't run into problems," she said.

Title: Cool Japan: Human fridge chills workers in extreme heat
Article:
HIGASHIOSAKA, (Japan): Feeling dizzy and unwell after cycling to work in Japan's punishing summer heat, warehouse worker Isao Tabuchi headed for his company's newest acquisition: a refrigerator for humans.
The phonebooth-sized machine, where jets of chilled air ensure ice-cold comfort, only launched this year but has proved popular in a country that seems to be getting inexorably warmer.
"I was really able to recover thanks to that. Once you use it, it's very, very cool," Tabuchi, 51, told AFP in the western industrial city of Higashiosaka.
Tokyo-based industrial equipment distributor Trusco Nakayama said it has sold more than 300 units of the "Do Hiemon Box" since April, priced at 1.5 million yen ($9,400).
Customers include construction sites, factories and warehouses, and will expand in the future to golf courses, said company sales agent China Yamamoto. Baseball stadiums may also be interested.
Some within the company had been sceptical, she added.
"It's large, it's expensive, and it's not the kind of product where you can just explain it in words and have customers say, 'Okay, let's buy one.' So there were a lot of uncertainties," she told AFP.
- 'Cruelly hot' -
Scientists say human-induced climate change is increasing the frequency and intensity of extreme heat events around the world.
In 2025, Japan saw its hottest summer on record.
This year, the weather office began using a new word — "kokushobi" or "cruelly hot day" — when temperatures hit 40C (104F), urging the public to treat extreme heat like a natural disaster.
Tokyo alone recorded almost 120 heat-related deaths in the month to mid-August, while close to 63,000 people nationwide this summer needed emergency care.
Since last year, Japanese businesses have faced tougher legal requirements to help employees toiling in the heat.
Building sites, for example, must provide workers with suitable clothing such as jackets with built-in fans, as well as air-conditioned break rooms and canopies to ensure shade.
A new initiative introduced this year allows bureaucrats in Tokyo to come to work in shorts — a groundbreaking move in a country where formal business attire still rules.
The impact of rising temperatures on businesses in the world's fourth-biggest economy is real.
A survey in July by Teikoku Databank found that 50 per cent of companies said intense heat had disrupted their operations.
Almost 88 percent said they had upgraded efforts to help workers cope with the heat.
- Vital investment -
The Do Hiemon Box can provide one line of defence.
It operates from a regular power socket, can be wheeled around and doesn't use much power, according to its maker.
To prevent overuse, it automatically shuts off after 20 minutes.
Investing in heat-countering measures has become essential to maintain the existing workforce and attract new recruits, said Yutaka Kono from Konoe, the specialist wholesaler of screws and surveying equipment where Tabuchi works.
Conventional air conditioners and spot coolers offer relief, but Kono's firm has many open areas to allow trucks and heavy equipment to operate.
"I was really surprised by this new concept of putting people into a kind of refrigerator, and I found it very appealing that by going inside that refrigerator, a person's body can be cooled in an instant to a safe temperature," Kono told AFP.
"That made me think, 'We definitely want to install one of these'," he said.
Worker Taichi Konishi, 24, says he uses it about three times a day.
After moving heavy boxes of metal tools and parts by hand between cargo pallets, he strolls over, steps into the box, sits down and smiles, running his fingers through his hair like in the shower.
"This feels really good," he told AFP.
"I've only been in for about two minutes, but even that was enough for all my sweat to dry up." — AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: India lifts four-year-long ban on wheat exports
Article:
NEW DELHI: India has lifted a four-year-long ban on exports of wheat and wheat products in a bid to boost farmers' incomes, the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) announced in an official notification, reported Xinhua.
The ban was imposed in May 2022. The export policy of wheat was revised from prohibited to free with immediate effect, the DGFT's notification said.
The lifting of the ban was significant, as the federal government said there were enough stocks of the commodity in the country and that it was a step towards encouraging the farming community to increase wheat production in the coming years.
According to official figures, India produced nearly 120.65 million tonnes of wheat during the country's crop year 2025-26 (July 2025-June 2026), about 2.3 per cent more than the previous crop year.
Commenting on the decision to lift the ban, the country's Food and Public Distribution Secretary Sanjeev Chopra reportedly said that since domestic wheat prices were currently depressed, allowing exports of wheat and wheat products would increase domestic prices, thus boosting farmers' incomes and encouraging good sowing in the forthcoming season.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MCA will not cooperate with DAP in polls, says sec-gen
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: MCA will not cooperate with DAP in upcoming elections, including the next Melaka polls, says secretary-general Datuk Chong Sin Woon.
Chong said although the Barisan Nasional leadership will decide on whether it contests the Melaka polls on its own or with another coalition, the state chapter's views will be prioritised.
"However, MCA will remain firm in not cooperating with DAP," he said when contacted.
Chong said MCA's stance was in line with a resolution passed at its annual general assembly last year.
Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh previously signalled a preference for BN to cooperate with Perikatan Nasional rather than Pakatan Harapan for the Melaka polls, mirroring a cooperation model seen during the Negri Sembilan election.
Previously, BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said that any decision on
political alliances
must account for local sentiment.
He said that the political reality in Melaka may differ significantly from Johor or Negri Sembilan, requiring an approach tailored to the grassroots.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Hot weather alert issued for 17 areas including Perak and Sabah
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) today issued a Level 1 hot weather alert for 17 areas across Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak.
In a statement, MetMalaysia said 11 of the affected areas are in Peninsular Malaysia, involving Larut and Matang, Kuala Kangsar, Kampar and Batang Padang in Perak; Kuala Krai in Kelantan; Kuantan, Raub, Temerloh and Pekan in Pahang; as well as Hulu Selangor and Gombak in Selangor.
Five areas in Sabah placed under the same status are Telupid, Tenom, Sandakan, Pitas and Beluran, while Marudi is the only affected area in Sarawak.
MetMalaysia said the Level 1 hot weather alert is issued when the maximum daily temperature in an area reaches between 35 and 37 degrees Celsius for at least three consecutive days.
The public can refer to MetMalaysia's official website for the latest daily hot weather updates nationwide. -- BERNAMA
